title: Robinson and Archer Demolish Pakistan as England Seize Control at Lord's
excerpt: Ollie Robinson's stunning 4-11 and Jofra Archer's 94mph hostility bowl Pakistan out for 110 as England build 261-run lead in second Test
body:
• Ollie Robinson took 4 for 11 from 13 overs with an economy rate of 0.84 as Pakistan were bowled out for 110 at Lord's
  • Jofra Archer clocked 94mph and took 3-26, bowling one of England's quickest new-ball spells on record
  • England lead by 261 runs heading into day three, with Emilio Gay unbeaten on 30 in the second innings

Ollie Robinson produced one of the most miserly bowling performances in recent Test history, taking 4 for 11 from 13 overs as Pakistan collapsed to 110 all out on day two of the second Test at Lord's on Friday, leaving England in total command with a 261-run lead.

Robinson's astonishing accuracy — six maidens, an economy rate of 0.84 — combined with Jofra Archer's raw pace to devastate a Pakistan batting order already weakened by the absence of opener Imam-ul-Haq, who was ruled out after straining his calf while fielding on day one.

Pakistan's Batting Order Crumbles

The visitors' innings lasted just 37.2 overs. Only rookie opener Azan Awais showed genuine resistance with a gritty 46 from 106 balls, surviving a dropped catch by Harry Brook at second slip on eight. No other Pakistan batter reached 20.

Archer set the tone with a searing opening spell, dismissing Shan Masood — opening in place of Imam — with a delivery clocked at 91mph that caught the edge. He averaged 90.7mph during his new-ball burst, ranked as the quickest opening spell yet recorded for England.

"It's really nice having the extra seamers in the line-up. I could play until I'm 40 at this rate."

— Jofra Archer, England fast bowler

Captain Babar Azam, returning after missing the first Test at Headingley with a finger injury, managed just 8 before Josh Tongue had him caught by Jordan Cox at third slip. Robinson then took over, dismissing Saud Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan lbw on review before a devastating double-wicket over accounted for Awais and Khurram Shahzad.

England's Tail Wags First

Earlier, England's last-wicket pair of Gus Atkinson (45) and Josh Tongue (30 not out) frustrated Pakistan with a partnership of 47, extending the first innings to a competitive 290. Mohammad Abbas finished with 4 for 73 but his earlier dominance — England had been 120 for 5 on day one — was gradually undone.

In their second innings, England reached 81 for 3 before bad light stopped play. Emilio Gay was unbeaten on 30, with Harry Brook on 7 not out. Khurram Shahzad (2-26) and Mohammad Ali provided Pakistan's only encouragement, but England's lead already appears insurmountable.

Series Context

Pakistan have now failed to bat 50 overs in any innings across the series, having been dismissed for 171 and 136 in an innings-and-103-run defeat at Headingley last week. England are on course for their first home Test series victory in two years.

The match has drawn large crowds at Lord's, including significant numbers from Britain's South Asian communities. Pakistan's struggles under captain Babar Azam — who has now scored just 8 in his only innings of the series — will concern fans ahead of a packed schedule that includes tours to Australia and India later this year.

What's Next

Rain is forecast for day three on Saturday, which could delay England's push for victory. But with a 261-run lead and seven second-innings wickets in hand, the hosts need only a few sessions to wrap up the match and take an unassailable 2-0 series lead with one Test remaining.
